BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SCAFFOLD DESIGN

This document describes the structural design of a Cantilever scaffold required for maintenance of the Fender at Jetty 1 / B. The scaffold envelope is 6.8m x 2.2m x 7.3m (length x width x height) and is configured with standards, ledgers, transoms, bracing, platforms, access, and support/tie arrangements as indicated on the approved drawing.

SAFE WORKING LOAD (SWL): 1.5 kN/m²

Note: This is a category 1 engineered scaffold. Scaffold shall be inspected and approved for use by assurance engineer before tagging for use.

GENERAL NOTE
BS EN 12811-1, 4.2.1.2 / 10.3.2.2 Scaffold tube material has a minimum nominal yield strength of 235 N/mm² (BS EN 12811-1, 4.2.1.2). A partial safety factor γM = 1.1 (BS EN 12811-1, 10.3.2.2) has been applied, giving a design resistance of 213.6 N/mm² used in member capacity checks. This design calculation was carried out in accordance with the limit states design method stipulated in EN 1993-1-1:2005 (Eurocode 3 - Design of Steel Structures).
Material Properties

48.3 mm outside diameter x 3.6 mm thick steel tube was defined by STAAD.Pro Connect Edition V22 section tables (British) and assigned to all scaffold members as section PIP483.6.

Modelling Philosophy
BS EN 12811-1, 10.2.3.2 / 10.2.3.3 A 3-D model was analysed using STAAD.Pro CONNECT Edition (V22) in compliance with EN 1993-1-1:2005. Base supports are modelled as pinned with lateral spring stiffness representing frictional restraint (KFX/KFZ = 23.588 kN). Base supports are modelled as elastic spring supports, restrained laterally in both horizontal directions with rotational degrees of freedom released, representing flexible ground contact conditions at each standard foot. See Appendix A for model views.

COUNTERWEIGHT STABILITY CHECK — EQU LIMIT STATE (EN 1990)
Basis: Cantilever analysis-line moment balance about the pivot line per EN 1990 EQU limit state. Negative vertical support reactions from STAAD ULS combinations represent hold-down demand at backspan nodes. ULS action factors (destabilising: 1.5, stabilising CW: 0.9) are already embedded in the STAAD combinations; no additional multiplier is applied here.

Counterweight verified by ULS global moment equilibrium. Maximum ULS hold-down demand at backspan base node 21 = 4.030 kN (LC 46). This is an EQU partial-factor artefact — the overall overturning is resisted by the counterweight moment; no base anchorage to the supporting structure is required provided the counterweight is maintained in position. Ensure counterweight is physically secured and in place before any live loading is applied.
Full design procedure is documented in Appendix F.

CONCLUSION
The structural analysis and design of the Cantilever scaffold confirms the structure is adequate for its intended purpose. All member utilization ratios are below unity (maximum UC = 0.661 at Member 293). Vertical and horizontal deflections are within their respective allowable limits of L/100 = 18.0mm and L/200 = 13.5mm. All scaffold tube coupler connections are adequate for the applied axial loads.
RECOMMENDATIONS
The scaffold shall be inspected by a competent Scaffold Inspector after erection to confirm conformity with the design specification and approved working drawings before use. All erection work shall comply with the design intent and material specification. Any proposed change to the design requires a re-design and the Scaffold Engineer shall be duly informed.
INSTALLATION NOTES
  1. The scaffold working drawings and purpose of the scaffold must be reviewed and discussed by all personnel involved prior to execution.
  2. Confirm that the Cantilever scaffold configuration matches the approved drawing and is suitable for maintenance.
  3. The work vicinity must be barricaded and appropriate signage placed at all access points.
  4. All scaffolders must wear complete PPE in accordance with NLNG work-at-height regulations.
  5. A valid work permit must be obtained, discussed, and signed before erection commences.
  6. Scaffold erection must be carried out in strict accordance with NASC guidance and site safety procedures.
  7. Install and secure cantilever support members, needles, anchors, ties, and back-span restraints exactly as shown on the approved drawing before building the working platform.
  8. Build the scaffold frame to the approved envelope of 6.8m x 2.2m x 7.3m, checking level, plumb, and cantilever projection at each lift.
  9. Install bracing, ledgers, transoms, platform boards, guardrails, and toe boards progressively, maintaining all specified ties and restraints.
  10. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 0.8m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  11. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 1.3m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  12. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 2.3m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  13. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 2.8m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  14. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 3.3m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  15. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 4.3m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  16. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 4.6m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  17. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 5.3m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  18. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 5.6m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  19. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 6.5m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  20. Install mid-level horizontal ledgers and transoms at 7.0m height in accordance with the working drawing.
  21. Install all plan, face, and longitudinal bracing shown on the approved drawing to provide sway resistance in both principal directions.
  22. Install platform boards, guardrails, mid-rails, toe boards, access arrangements, and any handrail load-resisting members required by the design.
  23. Tighten and torque-check all load-bearing couplers and support connections before the scaffold is released for inspection.
  24. The scaffold structure must be inspected and tagged by a competent advance scaffold inspector after erection and before use.
  25. The safe working load (SWL) stated on the design report must not be exceeded at any time during operations.
  26. All modifications made after erection must be carried out by a competent scaffold team with the approval of the scaffold engineer. End-user or third-party modification of this scaffold structure is strictly prohibited.
  27. For dismantling, perform the erection steps in reverse order.

APPENDIX F — COUNTERWEIGHT DESIGN CALCULATION (A–Z)
Design approach: An initial counterweight estimate of 1 kN/m² applied uniformly over the counterweight zone was used for the first STAAD analysis run. This is the standard iterative procedure — a non-trivial initial load is necessary to obtain meaningful support reactions, from which the actual counterweight demand is then derived by moment equilibrium (see F.3). The member loads shown in F.5 represent the final design values applied in the current STAAD model.
F.1 — Design Basis
EN 1990:2002 EQU The scaffold is a cantilever arrangement. Imposed loads on the overhang create an overturning moment about the support edge. Stability is verified at the Equilibrium (EQU) limit state per EN 1990:2002 — the appropriate limit state where loss of static equilibrium governs over material failure. The EQU partial factors embedded in the STAAD ULS combinations are:
• Destabilising permanent action (DL): γdst = 1.5
• Destabilising variable action (LL, WL): γdst = 1.5
• Stabilising permanent action (CW): γstb = 0.9

The check is satisfied when the stabilising moment from the counterweight — at its reduced factored value — equals or exceeds the overturning moment from all destabilising actions at their amplified values. This is assessed through the STAAD ULS combination results.
F.2 — Geometry: Pivot Line, Counterweight Zone and Lever Arm
STAAD model geometry Pivot line: The row of base support nodes at the edge of the supporting structure about which overturning is assessed — nodes 23, 38, 24, located at Z = 4.0 m.

Counterweight zone: The plan polygon on the backspan platform designated for kentledge placement, bounded by nodes 41, 53, 54, 46 at elevation y = 1.0 m.
Zone plan area:  ACW = 1.8 m²

Zone centroid (geometric centre of the polygon) at Z = 0.5 m.

Lever arm (perpendicular distance from CW centroid to pivot line):
LCW = |0.5  − 4.0| = 3.5 m
F.3 — Overturning Moment and Minimum Required Counterweight
Moment balance method Vertical base support reactions (FY) are read from the STAAD output for every ULS combination across all base nodes. STAAD sign convention: positive FY = upward push from ground (compression); negative FY = structure lifting off — a hold-down demand at that node.

For each ULS combination, every node showing negative FY contributes to the overturning moment about the pivot line:
Moverturn = Σ (|FY,i| × di)
where di is the perpendicular distance from node i to the pivot line (m).

The minimum counterweight required to stabilise the moment at that analysis line:
CWmin,line = Moverturn ÷ (γstb × LCW)

This is evaluated at each distinct row of base nodes (analysis line) independently for every ULS combination. The line-by-line CWmin values within a given combination are summed to obtain the total counterweight demand for that combination — each analysis line represents a separate strip of the scaffold base, and summing across all strips gives the total counterweight required to stabilise the structure as a whole. The combination producing the largest total demand is the governing case; the minimum design counterweight equals that total. Results for the governing combination are tabulated below.
Analysis Line Governing LC Critical Node(s) Σ Overturning Moment, M (kNm) γstb CWmin = M ÷ (γstb × 3.5 m)
Z = 0 m LC 44 21 9.912 0.9 9.912 ÷ (0.9 × 3.5) = 3.147 kN
Z = 0.6 m LC 44 28 5.56 0.9 5.56 ÷ (0.9 × 3.5) = 1.765 kN
Z = 1.2 m LC 44 27 5.004 0.9 5.004 ÷ (0.9 × 3.5) = 1.589 kN
Z = 1.8 m LC 44 26 10.532 0.9 10.532 ÷ (0.9 × 3.5) = 3.343 kN
Minimum Design Counterweight = Σ CWmin across all lines (LC 44): 9.844 kN  (1.003 t)
F.4 — Design Counterweight
Target value The counterweight is sized at the calculated minimum:
CWdesign = CWmin = 9.844 kN (1.003 t)

This is the minimum kentledge mass required within the designated zone to satisfy EQU overturning equilibrium across all ULS combinations. It is used as the basis for STAAD load distribution.
F.5 — Distribution of Counterweight Load to STAAD Members
Load distribution The counterweight is represented in STAAD as UDL (kN/m) member loads on horizontal members within the CW zone. The equivalent uniform pressure over the zone is first determined:

qCW = CWdesign ÷ ACW = 9.844 ÷ 1.8 = 5.469 kN/m²

Each horizontal member carries load proportional to its tributary width (edge members: half the adjacent bay width; interior members: sum of adjacent half-bays):
w = qCW × btributary
Member(s) Role Tributary Width, b w = 5.469 × b  (kN/m)
Members 73, 75, 76, 88, 89, 90 Edge 0.500 / 2 = 0.250 m 5.469 × 0.25 = 1.367 kN/m
Members 81, 82, 83 Interior (0.250 + 0.250) = 0.500 m 5.469 × 0.5 = 2.734 kN/m
Total applied to zone members: 9.844 kN
These UDL GY (downward) loads are applied in STAAD under LC 7, declared as LOADTYPE Dead. This classification causes the EQU stabilising factor of 0.9 to be applied automatically in the ULS combinations, consistent with EN 1990 Table A1.2(A). Refer to Appendix G for the applicable design standards.
F.6 — Residual Hold-down Demand at Backspan Base Nodes
EQU partial factor effect Under ULS EQU combinations, the destabilising factor (1.5) exceeds the stabilising CW factor (0.9). As a consequence, backspan base nodes close to the pivot line may continue to register negative FY in the STAAD output even with a correctly sized counterweight in place. This is a mathematical consequence of the EQU factor distribution — not an indication of counterweight inadequacy.

The governing verification criterion is global moment equilibrium about the pivot line, demonstrated in G.3 above. The maximum residual hold-down demand recorded at any single base node is 4.03 kN at node 21, LC 46 (ULS 1.5DL + 1.5LL + 1.5WLZ + 0.9CW). The counterweight provides the necessary global stabilising moment; no structural anchorage of the scaffold base to the supporting surface is required, provided the counterweight remains in position throughout the working life of the scaffold.
